items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, opening with the slogan about the top arrow of a magic diagram: for morphisms f : X -> Z, g : Y -> Z and Z -> T of algebraic spaces over S, the induced morphism i : X x_Z Y -> X x_T Y is representable, locally of finite type, locally quasi-finite, separated and a monomorphism, and becomes an immersion, a closed immersion or quasi-compact under local separatedness, separatedness or quasi-separatedness of Z -> T (source lines 505-522). The proof identifies the defining square as a fibre product, which exhibits i as the base change of the diagonal Delta_{Z/T}; all four assertions then follow from the properties of the diagonal recorded earlier in the chapter and the translation principle for representable morphisms.
